Subject: Pricing question — baseline spend & burst rates

Hi Rachel,

Quick one from procurement as we map vendor options for our analytics platform. Can you confirm Redwood's standard stance on: 

- Minimum monthly spend if we want committed discount tiers (do you require a dollar commit or token baseline?)
- Overage/burst rate when we exceed commit (is it priced as a multiple of on-demand or at a flat on-demand rate?)
- Whether unused commit credits roll over month-to-month or if there's a true-up quarterly?
- Typical tier discounts for hosted API volume (ballpark %) at 1M, 5M, 20M tokens/month?

We pulled a small usage sample (attached) to get a sense of our footprint. Procurement is asking for a concise term summary they can put in our SOW/PO. If useful, we can schedule a 30m call this week.

Thanks —
Olivia

olivia@acmeanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Pricing question — baseline spend & burst rates

Hi Olivia — thanks for the data, that helps. High-level answers below; see inline for options and a provisional sheet attached. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer.

Summary (options):
1) On-demand (no commit): progressive volume discounts by monthly token bands; typical ballparks we offer to similar customers: ~8% at ~1M tokens/mo, ~12% at ~5M, ~18% at 20M+. No minimum spend required.

2) Baseline commit (monthly $ or token equivalent): standard mid-market commits start around $25k/mo (token equivalent) and come with higher guaranteed discounts (typically 10–15% for that band). Commits buy predictability and extended capacity guarantees.

3) Overage / burst handling: we can support bursts above baseline. Two common patterns we use:
   - Overage billing: excess tokens billed at a premium multiplier of on-demand (typical range 1.25x–1.5x depending on discount depth).
   - Burst cap + protection: allow short-term burst up to a multiple (e.g., 2x) of baseline for limited windows; those tokens can be billed at an intermediate premium and not counted against the commit for true-up purposes.

4) Rollover / true-up: preferred approach is quarterly true-up (no month-to-month rollover). Customer can pick monthly vs quarterly true-up during contracting; quarterly true-up is common for smoothing.

Attached: provisional_pricing_sheet.xlsx — includes a model using your Q1 sample.

Proposed next step: if procurement wants a clean term summary for PO, we can propose a 6-month pilot with a contracted baseline ($25k/mo) that gives you a 12% token discount and a burst allowance (2x baseline for short windows at 1.35x on-demand). Post-pilot we can true-up and move to an annual commit if that looks good.

I'll loop in Sales Ops / Finance internally to confirm the exact overage multiplier we can offer for a first-time pilot.

Best,
Rachel
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisional_pricing_sheet.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-06T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing question — baseline spend & burst rates

Looping in a recommended term we can offer to get the deal over the line quickly. Rachel — feel free to use the language below in the term sheet.

Suggested pilot commercial (internal approved range):
- Pilot term: 6 months
- Baseline commit: $25,000 per month (token equivalent).
- Discount on baseline: 12% effective vs on-demand list.
- Overage (sustained): billed at 1.25x on-demand for token usage beyond baseline in the same billing period.
- Burst allowance: up to 2x baseline for up to 10 short windows/month (first 30 minutes of an incident window) billed at 1.4x on-demand; these are defined as "burst windows" and won't reduce the committed bucket for quarterly true-up purposes.
- True-up cadence: quarterly — unused committed tokens do not roll over beyond quarter.

Notes: Finance wants a clear cap on burst minutes and a documented definition of a burst window to avoid open-ended exposure. If Acme is comfortable with a clearly defined burst window policy we can accept a slightly lower overage multiplier.

Marissa
Head of Growth — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing question — baseline spend & burst rates

Adding a couple practical guardrails from ops/legal to keep the commercial safe for both sides: 

- Tiered overage: if monthly sustained overage exceeds 50% of baseline for more than 2 consecutive months, we propose a short re-evaluation (true-up) to move to a higher commit band rather than sustained overage billing.
- No rollover: confirmed — unused committed tokens expire at quarter end (no monthly carry-forward).
- Burst policy: define "burst window" as a contiguous 30-minute period initiated by the customer's request or detected incident; maximum 10 such windows/month. Bursts inside those windows billed at the agreed burst multiplier.
- SLA note: for capacity-sensitive customers we'll want a 72-hour notice approach for predictable capacity increases; ad-hoc bursts are supported but subject to availability across regions.

Markus has signaled initial approval for the pilot-level discount; I'll get Finance to sign off on the exact 1.25x vs 1.35x overage options depending on burst definition.

Karthik

Hi Olivia — following internal review, here is a consolidated term summary you can share with procurement / legal. If this looks OK we'll issue a short term-sheet and draft SOW.

Consolidated pilot proposal (6 months):
- Baseline: $25,000 / month (token equivalent) — 12% discount vs on-demand list.
- Overage (sustained excess within billing period): 1.25x on-demand.
- Burst windows: Up to 10 burst windows/month, each up to 30 minutes, allowed up to 2x baseline for the duration of a burst window; burst tokens billed at 1.4x on-demand and excluded from quarterly true-up accounting.
- True-up: Quarterly true-up; unused committed tokens do not roll over beyond quarter.
- Re-evaluation trigger: if overage >50% of baseline for 2 consecutive months, parties will review and discuss moving to a higher commit band.
- SLA/Capacity: We can support region US with 72-hour notice for predictable capacity increases; ad-hoc bursts subject to availability.

Attachments: RDW_Acme_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term summary), provisional_pricing_sheet.xlsx previously attached.

Next step: if Acme is good with these pilot terms, procurement can issue the PO to the billing address in the term-sheet; otherwise, let me know which items you'd like to adjust and we can route for final approvals.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
